paragraphs.text: The lot came forth, up, or out {Jos 19:1; Jos 19:10; Jos 19:17} of the bosom, lap, {Pro 16:33} pot, or some other vessel in use for that purpose; for the manner of this lottery is not expressed: but that it was solemnly done with fasting and prayer premised, is probable; {Jdg 20:26 Act 1:24} and that it was ordered by a divine providence, is certain. {Pro 16:33} And hence it was that Judah’s lot came out first, and fell out in the best part of the land: to show that God had a purpose to exalt that tribe above the rest.
paragraphs.anchor: This then was the lot of the tribe, &c.

paragraphs.text: See Num 34:2. Where God doth, as it were, draw a map of Canaan, and showeth the bounds of it on every side.
Heb., From the tongue: some render it from the promontory running out into the sea, in form of a tongue.
paragraphs.anchor: From the bay that looketh southward.

paragraphs.text: i.e., To the ascent of scorpions, or of the mountains that were crooked as scorpions, or that abounded with scorpions. {Jdg 1:36}
A city whence that wilderness, not the same with that of Sin or Sinai, had its name.
These two places are {Num 34:4} called Hazaraddar.
paragraphs.anchor: To Hezron, and went up to Adar.

paragraphs.text: It is God that "determineth the times before appointed, and the bounds of our habitations"; {Act 17:26} the walls of his people’s houses are continually before him. {Isa 49:16}
paragraphs.anchor: This shall be your south coast.

paragraphs.text: The lake of Sodom, into which the river Jordan runneth, and there endeth.
Which had its name for some unknown reason: so Migdalgad. {Jos 15:37}
Or, The fuller’s well; who hath his name in Hebrew from footing it, quia pedibus mundet vestes. So hath the talebearer. {Psa 15:3}
Where with barbarous cruelty they sacrificed their children to Moloch, or Saturn. {2Ki 23:11} Hence Gehenna for hell.
paragraphs.anchor: By the valley of the son of Hinnon.

paragraphs.text: Anciently Jebus, {Jdg 19:11} afterwards Jerusalem; not quasi ιερον σολυμων vel σολομωντος, as Hegesippus dreameth, but of Jireh, {Gen 22:14} "he will provide," and Shalom, "peace." The Hebrew here and elsewhere writeth it in the dual form, as it were the double Jerusalem, the higher and the lower town, from which the apostle gathereth an allegory. {Gal 4:15}
i.e., Urbs nemorum. Vat.
Not that of the Idumeans, but another of that name, from its roughness.
Where Beelzebub was worshipped. Hence Acheron for hell,
“ Fiectere si nequeo superos, Acheronta movebo. ” - Virg.
i.e., The midland sea, great in comparison of the lakes of Palestine, called also seas.
See Jos 14:13.
Nos quoque militemus, Heaven is not to be had sine sanguine et sudore, without pains, patience, violence.

Which signifieth a city of books, as Debir doth a secret and sacred place. Some think it was a University, or at least, that there was a famous library, such as was afterwards the Serapion at Alexandria, furnished with the best books by Ptolomy Philadelph, who was φιλολογωτατος βασιλευς, as Cyril noteth, a great lover of learning.
paragraphs.anchor: And the name of Debir before was Kirjathsepher.

paragraphs.text: Yet with her consent, who as she was not to be forced, {Gen 24:51; Gen 24:57} so she might not refuse without reason, and say -
paragraphs.anchor: To him will I give Achsah my daughter.

paragraphs.text: “ Non amo te Sabidi, nec possum dicere quare. ” - Martial.
So that Othniel and Achsah were brothers’ children. Hence some infer the lawfulness of such marriages now.
paragraphs.anchor: The son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb.

paragraphs.text: Or, She moved her husband that she might ask another field. Covetousness is never contented, but still craving more, as the horse leeches’ daughters. Othniel hardly yielded to this motion, but she would have it so, and therefore lighted off her ass, either as discontented, or as desirous to present her request.
i.e., Other lands well watered, whence we may derive water to the rest.
paragraphs.anchor: Give me also springs of water

paragraphs.text: What can a kind father deny his child? And shall not God give his dear children "upper and nether springs," blessings of both lives, bona throni et bona scabelli? and are they not worthily miserable that will not make themselves happy by asking? How confidently came Esau to his father for a blessing, and the prodigal for a child’s part! Now if men which are evil do give good things to their children that ask them: how much more will your heavenly Father? &c. See what he saith, {Isa 45:11} "Ask me of things to come concerning" (or on the behalf of) "my sons, and concerning the work of my hands command ye me." Oh that we did but understand the latitude of this royal charter!
paragraphs.anchor: And he gave her the upper springs, and the nether springs.
